Multiview spatial models of feature expression (MISTy)

Source: R/misty.R
runMisty.Rd

Fits MISTy, the multiview model of Tanevski et al. (2022, Genome Biology 23:97), on the cells of a Giotto object. For every target feature it measures how much of the target's variation is explained by the other features of the same cell (intraview), by the sum over the cell's immediate neighbours (juxtaview), by a distance-weighted sum over its wider neighbourhood (paraview) and, optionally, by the cell-type composition of both neighbourhoods and by other feature types or enrichment scores. It is the algorithm of the mistyR package (run_misty() with random_forest_model or linear_model, then collect_results()): the same view models, seeds, cross-validation, meta-model, p-values and result tables, so mistyR's plot_*() functions draw its output. One model is fitted on the whole slide, or one per sample (e.g. per FOV) with sample_by.

It runs on all cells, also of whole slides and GiottoDisk-backed objects: only the features used are read, cells are matched to their positions by cell ID, neighbourhoods come from Giotto spatial networks and every view is a sparse product (cost linear in the number of cells and edges), and the meta-model's p-values are computed in closed form (mistyR's ridge::pvals() forms an N x N matrix, which limits it to about 20,000 cells).

Usage

runMisty(
  gobject,
  spat_unit = NULL,
  feat_type = NULL,
  expression_values = c("normalized", "scaled", "custom"),
  targets = NULL,
  feats_to_use = NULL,
  spat_loc_name = NULL,
  coord_scale = 1,
  juxta_radius = 15,
  juxta_network = NULL,
  para_l = 20,
  para_family = c("gaussian", "exponential", "linear", "constant"),
  para_cutoff = NULL,
  para_zoi = 0,
  para_nn = NULL,
  para_network = NULL,
  composition = NULL,
  extra_views = NULL,
  sample_by = NULL,
  min_cells = 200L,
  model = c("random_forest", "linear"),
  bypass_intra = FALSE,
  cv_folds = 10L,
  num_trees = 100L,
  mtry = NULL,
  sample_fraction = NULL,
  cores = NA,
  seed = 42L,
  results_folder = NULL,
  name = "misty",
  view = NULL,
  return_gobject = TRUE,
  verbose = NULL
)

Arguments

gobject

giotto object

spat_unit

spatial unit

feat_type

feature type of the targets and of the intra-, juxta- and paraview

expression_values

expression values of feat_type to model

targets

features of feat_type to model. NULL (default): all of feats_to_use, or all features when both are NULL.

feats_to_use

features of feat_type in the intraview, juxtaview and paraview, i.e. the predictors. Must include targets. NULL (default): targets.

spat_loc_name

name of the spatial locations. NULL: the default.

coord_scale

numeric > 0. Factor that converts the spatial coordinates to the units of juxta_radius, para_l, para_cutoff and para_zoi (e.g. 0.12028 for CosMx pixels to micrometres).

juxta_radius

numeric or NULL. Juxtaview: sum over the Delaunay neighbours (deldir, as mistyR) no farther than this distance. NULL: no juxtaview.

juxta_network

name of a stored spatial network of spat_unit to use for the juxtaview instead of a Delaunay network; its edges no longer than juxta_radius are kept.

para_l

numeric (one or more) or NULL. Paraview: sum over the other cells weighted by para_family with length scale para_l, one paraview per value. NULL: no paraview.

para_family

weight of a cell at distance d: "gaussian" exp(-d^2 / l^2), "exponential" exp(-d / l), "linear" max(0, 1 - d / l) or "constant" 1 (with para_nn nearest neighbours, round(l) when para_nn is NULL), as mistyR's add_paraview().

para_cutoff

numeric or NULL. Cells farther than para_cutoff * para_l are left out of the paraview (mistyR sums over all cells). NULL: 4 for "gaussian" and 16 for "exponential" (weights below 1.2e-7 are dropped), 1 for "linear" (exact).

para_zoi

numeric. Zone of indifference: cells closer than this get weight 0 in the paraview (mistyR's zoi).

para_nn

integer or NULL. Limit the paraview to the para_nn nearest neighbours of each cell (mistyR's nn).

para_network

name of a stored spatial network of spat_unit to use for the paraview neighbours instead of building one. Weights come from the distances; a kNN network is used as directed.

composition

NULL or a cell metadata column with a label per cell (e.g. cell types). Adds the juxtaview and paraview(s) of the one-hot labels: how many cells of each label are next to, or around, the cell.

extra_views

NULL or a named list of further predictor sources. Each element is a list with either feat_type (+ optional expression_values, default "normalized", and feats, default all; at most 500 features) or enrichment (the name of a spatial enrichment,

  • optional feat_type), and views, a subset of c("intra", "juxta", "para") (default c("juxta", "para")): the source's values in the cell itself, summed over the juxta neighbours, or weighted over the paraview.

sample_by

NULL (default) or a cell metadata column (e.g. "fov"). NULL fits one model per target on all cells (the whole slide); a column fits one model per target in each of its groups (samples), on views built from the whole slide. See Details.

min_cells

integer. With sample_by, samples with fewer cells (or fewer than cv_folds) are left out.

model

view model: "random_forest" (ranger, mistyR's random_forest_model: 100 trees, impurity importance, out-of-bag predictions) or "linear" (mistyR's linear_model: least squares, out-of-fold predictions, coefficients as importances).

bypass_intra

logical. Leave the intraview out of the meta-model (mistyR's bypass.intra): the intraview model becomes a constant, so multi.R2 is what the other views explain on their own.

cv_folds

integer. Folds of the cross-validated performance estimate and of the linear view models' out-of-fold predictions.

num_trees, mtry

random forest: number of trees and of features tried at each split (NULL: ranger's default, the square root of the number of predictors).

sample_fraction

random forest: share of the cells drawn (with replacement) for each tree. NULL (default) draws as many cells as there are, as ranger and mistyR do; a smaller share such as 0.1 fits large data several times faster.

cores

integer. Threads of each random forest. NA: Giotto's giotto.cores option. With a parallel future plan the targets (or, with sample_by, the samples) are instead fitted in parallel, one thread each; every worker loads the packages, so on one machine the threads usually match the workers' speed with less memory (per FOV on 146,000 cells: 7.8 min and 6.2 GB with 4 threads, 8.5 min and 11.7 GB with 4 workers).

seed

integer. Seed of the random forests and the folds (mistyR's default 42). The caller's random number state is restored on exit.

results_folder

NULL or a folder to write mistyR's result files to (coefficients.txt, performance.txt, importances_*.txt), which mistyR::collect_results() reads. With sample_by, one subfolder per sample.

name

prefix of the feature metadata columns

view

character. Name of a GiottoClass::giottoView slotted on gobject. Supplied, the object is narrowed once before the expression, spatial locations, cell metadata and enrichments are read, so the model uses the view's cells.

return_gobject

logical. Return the giotto object with the results in the feature metadata (default) or the result list.

verbose

be verbose

Value

With return_gobject = TRUE, the giotto object with <name>_intra_R2, <name>_multi_R2 and <name>_gain_R2 (in %, the mean over the cross-validation folds, and over the samples with sample_by) added to the feature metadata of feat_type (NA for features that are not targets). Otherwise a list shaped as mistyR::collect_results() returns it (data.frames improvements, contributions, importances, improvements.stats, contributions.stats, importances.aggregated), which mistyR's plot_improvement_stats(), plot_view_contributions(), plot_interaction_heatmap() and plot_interaction_communities() take. Its sample column is the value of sample_by; for a whole-slide model, the absolute path of results_folder, or name.

Details

For each target and each view a model predicts the target from the view's features: out-of-bag predictions for random forests, out-of-fold predictions for linear models. Like mistyR, a view built from feats_to_use (intra-, juxta- and paraview) leaves out the target's own column; composition and extra views keep all their columns. The meta-model regresses the target on the views' predictions: ordinary least squares when it has one predictor, otherwise ridge regression with the penalty chosen automatically (Cule and De Iorio 2012, as ridge::linearRidge() with lambda = "automatic", which mistyR uses). Its coefficients are the view contributions, with p-values of a normal test (ridge, as ridge::pvals()) or a t test (least squares). Performance is estimated by cv_folds-fold cross-validation of the meta-model (folds stratified by the target's quantiles, as caret::createFolds()): intra.R2 is the R2 of the intraview alone, multi.R2 that of all views, gain.R2 = multi.R2 - intra.R2 (in %; negative fold values are set to 0, as mistyR does), with RMSE versions and one-sided t tests of the gain (p.R2, p.RMSE). Importances are standardised per target and view and weighted by 1 - p-value of the view's contribution, as collect_results() does.

Whole slide or per sample: with sample_by, the views are built once from the whole slide (a cell's neighbours across a sample border still count) and the models are fitted on each sample's cells, as mistyR's run_misty() on each sample followed by collect_results(). The *.stats tables then hold means and standard deviations over the samples, and improvements one row per sample, so the gains can be mapped back onto the tissue. Per-sample models are MISTy's own design: each learns the relationships within one region, so differences between regions do not count as a neighbourhood effect, but each sees fewer cells (lower intra.R2, noisier for rare targets). A target that is constant in a sample is not fitted there.

Differences from mistyR: views are built from Giotto networks (Delaunay by deldir, dbscan radius or kNN searches) on positions matched by cell ID; the paraview is truncated at para_cutoff * para_l; the linear view models use cv_folds folds (mistyR's linear_model() always uses 10); the result files of a run with only the intraview have one column fewer than mistyR's. With the same views and settings the R2, contributions and importances equal mistyR's.

Cost: views are sparse products, linear in the number of cells and edges (about 130 edges per cell for a gaussian paraview with para_l = 20 um at cell densities of tissue). The models hold the views as dense matrices (cells x features of all views); a random forest with 100 trees on 146,000 cells and 21 predictors takes about 11 s with 4 threads, so a run costs about (targets x views) of those. Extra views are capped at 500 features each: select features (e.g. highly variable genes) or use enrichment scores.

Examples

g <- GiottoData::loadGiottoMini("visium")
feats <- head(fDataDT(g)[order(-perc_cells), feat_ID], 10)

res <- runMisty(g, targets = feats[1:2], feats_to_use = feats,
    juxta_radius = 300, para_l = 300, model = "linear",
    return_gobject = FALSE)
res$improvements.stats
